title: Fleet Rung 30 — THE CALIBRATED ENGINE (mm-volume v1.2.0): the projection runs on REALITY, not on the plan's guess. Q10 WHAT IS THE TRUE FILL SIZE? calibratedAvgSize reads the fill-ledger's REAL classified fills (µ-precise, direction-law parsed): 130 real fills measure 0.691 SBD average notional vs the 0.068 SBD planned notion — reality runs ~10× the plan. When the ledger speaks, the projection RUNS ON IT: projected volume 39.168 → 796.032 SBD/day (SBD/STEEM 398.016 + HBD/HIVE 398.016), conservative net 0.2886 → 2.6516 SBD/day. The prior size rides along (avgSizePriorSbd + source) — calibration is NEVER a silent rewrite; fallback chain real-fills → exec-runs-planned → law-assumption, every rung labeled. Q11 DOES THE SHARE MOVE? shareSeries reads the desk's OWN append-only plan ledger as the time series: last-K {at, sharePct} points per venue, sorted, corrupt-rows-dropped, capK=24 — dominance becomes a trend, not a single frame; the series lives in the book's time-born `series` namespace, excluded from the byte-stable payload (values deterministic, timestamps are the axis). Q12 WHAT DID CALIBRATION CHANGE? a calibration block carries prior→calibrated side-by-side with the lift % (+916.1765% at first light) — the owner sees the lift AND its source. The honest consequence is surfaced: the calibrated share at N=1 exceeds 100% (the capacity ladder saturates the measured pond — the saturates flag and the tape bound say so, never hidden).
